1. The present appeal is filed by the original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 31/12/2009 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Patan in Maniben Hemrajbhai Thakkar vs Ramsukh Kashiram Yadav on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189766853/

sentences.text:
Short facts of the claim case are as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1169/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 2.1.

On 15/09/1989, deceased Hemrajbhai Thakkar had borrowed jeep bearing registration no.GJ-8-61 of his relative Jayantibhai Mohanbhai and started for village Chanasma from Bhabhar at about 12:00 o'clock in the night.
He was accompanied by two other persons.

When he reached near village Sami at about 3:00 o'clock in the night at that time tanker bearing registration no.MWU-4590 came from the opposite side with full lights and therefore, Hemrajbhai stopped his jeep on the left side of the road.
Though the jeep was stopped on the left side of the road, the driver of the tanker dashed the tanker with the jeep and caused an accident.
In the said accident, Hemrajbhai has died and other two persons who accompanied him got severe injuries.
Seeing the said accident, driver of the tanker ran away.

2.2. The appellants-original claimants i.e. heirs and legal representatives of the deceased Hemrajbhai therefore filed claim petition under the provisions of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- against the respondents.

2.3. Vide the aforesaid impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the appellants-original claimants under Section 166 of the Act, 1988, holding 25% liability of the driver of the jeep, and held that the appellants-original claimants are entitled to receive an amount of Rs.1,45,725/- from the total amount of compensation of Rs.1,94,300/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1169/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined till its actual realization.

3. This Court vide order dated 18/06/2014, noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants- original claimants and the grounds raised in the present appeal, has admitted the appeal.
4. Learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants has submitted at length facts on the point of quantum of compensation.

He has further submitted that the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate the documentary evidence produced on record and vehemently argued that the deceased was running Janta Restaurant and Janta Video Center.

He has further referred the documentary evidence produced before the learned Tribunal and vehemently argued that the income of the deceased was Rs.5,000/- per month but the learned Tribunal failed to appreciate the documentary evidence and assessed only Rs.1,250/- which is not just and proper.
He has further submitted that the income of the deceased must be assessed as Rs.5,000/- per month.

4.1. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants- original claimants has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in passing the impugned judgment and award and has failed to Maniben Hemrajbhai Thakkar vs Ramsukh Kashiram Yadav on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189766853/
2 appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective.

sentences.text: He has further submitted that the Tribunal has not properly assessed the income of the deceased.

He has further submitted that the Tribunal has also erred in assessing multiplier of 13 without considering the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1169/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined age of the deceased about 45 years at the time of the accident.

He has submitted that as the deceased was aged about 45 years at the time of the accident, multiplier of 14 is required to be considered in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and the schedule prescribed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4.2. Learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants has further submitted that the Tribunal has erred in assessing 25% negligence of the deceased though he has stopped his vehicle on the left side of the road seeing the tanker coming from the opposite side in high speed and in rash and negligent manner.
He has also submitted that the learned tribunal has erred in not considering the arguments of the original claimants with regard to liability of payment of compensation.

He has submitted that as the owner of the jeep was paying additional premium for the driver, risk of the driver is covered under the additional premium and the insurance company of the jeep is liable for payment of the compensation.

4.3. Learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants has submitted that the learned Tribunal has also overlooked the settled principles of law in relation to the assessment of other conventional heads also.
The learned advocate for the appellants-claimants has therefore submitted that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable and it is required to be modified in accordance with law.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1169/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 5.

Learned advocates appearing for the other side have submitted that the learned Tribunal recorded the at length findings in para-13 of the judgment and vehemently argued that the claimants produced the old documentary evidence on record and tried to show more income of the deceased.

It is further submitted that in the year 1999, if the income of the deceased was more than Rs.20,000/-, the deceased must file the income tax return but the claimants have failed to produce any income tax return to prove the income of the deceased.

It is further submitted that there is no any reliable evidence to prove the income of the deceased and the learned Tribunal rightly fixed the income of deceased as Rs.1,250/- per month which is just and proper and not required to be interfered.

5.1. Learned advocates for the other side have submitted that the learned Tribunal, after appreciating the materials available on record, awarded the compensation under each head which is just, proper and reasonable and not required to be interfered in this appeal and lastly prayed to dismiss the present appeal.

6. Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and perused the record and proceedings and impugned judgment and award,
more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while passing the impugned Maniben Hemrajbhai Thakkar vs Ramsukh Kashiram Yadav on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189766853/
3 judgment and award.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the subject matter, the complainant Jagdishbhai-unarmed/armed Head Constable filed a complaint on the date of accident dated 15/09/1989.
The complaint is produced on record vide Exh.51 and the place of panchnama is produced vide Exh.52.
In the impugned judgment, the learned Tribunal recorded the findings on the point of negligence.
It appears from the record and findings that the learned Tribunal has appreciated the facts of place of panchnama vide Exh.52.
The learned Tribunal has further appreciated the fact that no evidence is produced of the charge sheet.
In other words, the original claimants have failed to produce the charge sheet documents.
The learned Tribunal has appreciated the evidence and recorded the findings that both the vehicles are liable in the said accident.
The learned Tribunal has further appreciated the oral evidence produced by the original claimants.
The truck driver has not entered into the witness box and then after assessed the negligence of the driver of both the vehicles.

The driver of the tanker is held negligent to the extent of 75% and the driver of the jeep (deceased) is held negligent to the extent of 25% which is just and proper and not required to be interfered in the said findings recorded by the learned Tribunal on the point of negligence.

Quantum of compensation:-
8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the subject matter, it appears from the record that the claimants have NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1169/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined produced the documentary evidence i.e. Janta Restaurant and Janta Video Center and also produced the receipt of the license fee deposited in the treasury.
All the documents are in the name of the deceased and it is required to be presumed that the deceased was running the business.
The claimants have not produced any books of accounts or copy of any income tax returns to prove the exact income of the deceased.
Considering the documentary evidence produced on record, the income of the deceased at least should be assessed as Rs.3,000/- per month which is just and proper and reasonable.
The learned Tribunal failed to appreciate the said important aspect at the time of fixing the income of the deceased and hence the said aspect is required to be interfered by this Court.
Accordingly income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.3,000/- per month.

8.1. As regards the future prospect is concerned, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, noticing the age of the deceased as 47 years, as accepted by the Tribunal, 25% amount can be considered towards the future prospects of the deceased.

considering the fact that the deceased was survived by four dependents, 1/4th deduction has been applied towards spend by the deceased on himself.
Thus, the calculation of the prospective income of the deceased at the rate of 25% is considered as Rs.3,000/- * 25% (Rs.750/-) = Rs.3,750/-.

reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and the scheduled prescribed, the Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of 13 in the facts of the case.

sentences.text: Thus, the future loss benefit is determined as Rs.2,813/-*12*13 (Multiplier) which comes to Rs.4,38,828/-.
This brings me to the issue of loss of consortium as prayed for by the learned advocate for the appellants- original claimants.

As rightly prayed for by the learned advocate for the appellant in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd (supra), the claimants would be entitled to enhance amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium to the tune of Rs.1,93,600/-
(Rs.48,400/- X 4).

Lastly, the amount to be awarded under the conventional heads, more particularly, funeral expenses and the loss of estate is also required to be reconsidered in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
The same is to be considered as Rs.18,150/- respectively.

Liability:-
9.

As regards the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants on the issue of liability, it is vehemently argued that the respondent National NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1169/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/08/2025 undefined Insurance Company received the additional premium of Rs.8/-.
It is further submitted that the National Insurance Company is liable to pay 25% of the awarded amount.
It is further submitted that the learned Tribunal has failed to consider the facts of the insurance policy and required to be interfered in the interest of justice.

9.1. Considering the submission made by learned advocate for the appellants, original claimants and the documentary evidence available on record, the copy of the insurance policy of the vehicle jeep involved in the said accident produced vide Exh.72.
9.2.
Considering the facts of the documentary evidence being the insurance policy, it appears that the insurance company received the additional premium of Rs.8/-.
Legal liability to paid driver as per the ENDMAT-16.
It appears that the National Insurance Company received the additional premium of the paid driver of the vehicle jeep.

Considering the facts of the claim petition, the appellant original claimants clearly stated in para-10 that on 15/09/1989, deceased Hemrajbhai proceeded for purchase of buffaloes in a vehicle jeep of his friend Jayantibhai Mohanlal and the deceased Hemrajbhai himself was driving the jeep.

Considering this important fact that the deceased Hemrajbhai was not a paid driver of the owner of the jeep of Jayantibhai Mohanlal, under the circumstances, the insurance company received the additional premium for legal liability to paid driver.
